subject: AvaTech inference economics — competitive validation & next tests
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sankha Rao <sankha@avatech.com>, procurement@avatech.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: AvaTech inference economics — competitive validation & next tests

Hi Sankha / procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great questions from your infra and ML platform teams. Per our conversation I wanted to capture a concise validation plan and the competitive points we think matter most for your internal TCO comparison vs Hyperscaler X and Vendor Y.

Recap (short):
- Primary goals: predictable per-1M token unit economics for customer-facing chat (avg 350 tokens/request), 99th pct latency <300ms for 95% of requests, and cold-start KV cache behavior for multi-tenant models.
- Competitive pressure: Hyperscaler X is quoting lower list price on GPU hours but has more restrictive batching defaults; Vendor Y claims higher batch efficiency but no KV cache sharing.

Proposed validation/tests (priority):
1) Per-1M tokens costing sheet: run a 1M token simulated workload (mix: 65% generation, 35% embeddings) and compare raw token cost + infra overheads (batching savings, cache hit delta). We attached a template (avatech-1M-token-unit-econ.xlsx).
2) Batching sensitivity: run two runs with identical traffic profile — (a) Hyperscaler default batching, (b) Redwood continuous batching with 40ms aggregation window. Report median/99th latency and tokens/sec.
3) KV cache hit rate sweep: measure effective token cost at 3 cache hit rates (10%, 40%, 70%) and report per-1M amortized KV storage + hit-savings. See kv-cache-hit-sensitivity.pdf for suggested measurement plan.
4) Fallback behavior: induce model OOM/saturation and validate graceful fallback to a cheaper model variant — measure SLA impact and request-level routing decisions.

Asks / next steps:
- Can your ML platform team provision a short-lived sandbox with a representative 10k-100k request trace we can replay? Prefer AWS us-west-2.
- Procurement: please confirm any constraints on benchmarking credentials / allowed IP ranges.
- Redwood will run the 1M token sim and share a filled unit-econ sheet, plus an internal cost-driver breakdown (batch latency tradeoffs, KV amortization assumptions).

I'll loop in Ben to lead the technical validation. Marissa — can you confirm whether a 2-week window starting Feb 8th works for your team for the formal run?

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment stubs: avatech-1M-token-unit-econ.xlsx (spreadsheet), kv-cache-hit-sensitivity.pdf (doc)

From: Sankha Rao <sankha@avatech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@avatech.com, ml-platform@avatech.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jan 2027 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AvaTech inference economics — competitive validation & next tests

Jordan,

Thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifications before we schedule: 

- Sandbox: we can provision a staging cluster in us-west-2 but need IP allowlist + a short AUP (we'll share).
- Workload: we can provide a 50k request trace (anonymized) with the token distribution you requested; is that sufficient to extrapolate to 1M?
- Metrics: procurement needs a breakdown that separates raw cloud GPU spend from software-layer savings (batching + cache). Can you make that explicit in the unit-econ sheet?

Two questions from ML platform: 
1) For ‘KV cache hit rate sweep’ — do you have tooling to emulate synthetic cache hits (e.g., prefix-replay) or do you need us to craft traffic with repeated contexts?
2) For fallback testing — what model variants would Redwood fall back to (same family quantized vs smaller family)? We need to capture any change in output quality for our eval team.

Procurement: we also want a simple price sensitivity chart (best-case, expected, worst-case) at 1M tokens. Can Redwood include that?

Best,
Sankha Rao
Head of ML Platform | AvaTech
sankha@avatech.com

Sankha / team,

Thanks — quick technical answers: 

1) Sandbox & replay: we can accept your 50k trace and run multiple scaled replays to reach 1M tokens; Redwood's replay tool supports "prefix grouping" to synthesize higher cache-hit scenarios (we'll document method). That answers the cache emulation Q.

2) Fallback model variants: Redwood can fall back to either (A) the same family quantized variant (8-bit/Q4) or (B) a smaller family with matched prompts (different generation characteristics). For the validation run we'll do both variants in separate runs and include BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity deltas so your eval team can see quality impact.

3) Unit-econ separation: Jordan's attached spreadsheet includes separate tabs for raw GPU spend and software-layer savings (batching delta, KV-savings, routing delta). I'll fill the assumed batch latency windows and the continuous-batching parameters we propose (40ms, 80ms) and show sensitivity.

Attachments referenced: avatech-1M-token-unit-econ.xlsx (filled template v1), kv-cache-hit-sensitivity.pdf (methodology).

Tentative timeline:
- Feb 8: Redwood starts replay runs (3x runs: baseline, continuous-batching-40ms, continuous-batching-80ms).
- Feb 10: Deliver initial unit-econ + per-run latency percentiles and cost drivers.
- Feb 12: Follow-up call with ML eval team to review quality metrics and pick preferred fallback variant.

Let us know if we should compress the timeline.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Internal summary / action items (posting into the thread for transparency):

Marissa: confirm commercial guardrails for the two-week proof window (trial credits, nondisclosure for sandbox). Also, procurement asked for a price sensitivity chart at 1M tokens — can you prepare a 3-scenario chart (best/expected/worst) that explicitly lists amortized infra vs software savings?

Ben: lead the replay runs (Feb 8 start). Deliverables: run artifacts (latency p50/p95/p99), per-run token throughput, and the filled unit-econ workbook by Feb 10. Please document the method we use to synthesize higher cache-hit traces (prefix grouping) so the Avatech team can reproduce.

Grace: own the fallback quality evaluation with the ML team — produce embedding-similarity and a short human-eval checklist for the Feb 12 call. Capture any edge-case latency regressions from quantized variants.

Sankha / Avatech: if you can send the anonymized 50k trace and the sandbox IP allowlist by Feb 3, we'll lock dates.

I'll update the HubSpot deal with these milestones and share the MAP doc (mutual-action-plan-avt.docx) once Marissa confirms approvals.

Thanks — brief call Monday if anyone wants to run through the playbook beforehand.
